history.dynasty: Vijayanagara Empire (under Achyuta Deva Raya); built by the brothers Virupanna Nayaka and Viranna, imperial governors
history.summary: NOTE: CSV town 'Anantapur' is approximate - the temple is at Lepakshi village, now in Sri Sathya Sai district (carved out of Anantapur in 2022), about 15 km from Hindupur and 120-140 km from Bengaluru. Built in 1538 CE by Virupanna Nayaka and Viranna during the reign of Achyuta Deva Raya, this is one of the finest examples of Vijayanagara architecture and is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India as a Monument of National Importance (it is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site). Its wonders: the famous hanging pillar in the Natya Mandapa that does not fully touch the ground (a cloth can be passed beneath it); a monolithic Nandi 27 feet long and 15 feet high, one of the largest in India; the Nagalinga (a linga wrapped by a seven-hooded serpent carved from a single stone); extensive frescoes in natural pigments on the mandapa ceilings depicting scenes from the epics and Puranas; and the Kalyana Mandapa (marriage hall) with its carved pillars. The Ramayana link: Jatayu, the vulture-king wounded by Ravana while defending Sita, fell here, and Rama is said to have addressed the dying bird with 'Le Pakshi' ('Rise, O bird') - giving the village its name.

name: Lepakshi Temple
town_description: Lepakshi is a small village in Sri Sathya Sai district (formerly Anantapur district), about 15 km from Hindupur and a popular 120-140 km day trip from Bengaluru (2.5-3 hours by road). Apart from the Veerabhadra temple complex, it is known for its handloom textiles. Visitors usually spend 2-3 hours in the complex; entry is free and guides are available locally.

travel.airport: Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru - about 120-140 km from Lepakshi.
travel.railway: Hindupur railway station, about 15 km away; connects to Bengaluru.
travel.road: About 120-140 km (2.5-3 hours) from Bengaluru via NH 44; regular buses and taxis from Hindupur and Bengaluru (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; early morning or late afternoon for comfortable weather and photography.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-6:00 PM daily (entry free; photography generally allowed in the complex, verify restrictions in sanctum).
